long_biography.plain_text:
Pueyo built his career around tourism rather than a single property. After helping develop the Mallorcan Royaltur project, he turned toward the Caribbean and entered Cancún during Mexico's mid-1980s financial crisis. He used a debt-swap financing opportunity to acquire beachfront land and launch Oasis, the first Spanish hotel brand established in the destination.

His approach combined resort ownership with travel agencies, charter aviation and later real-estate interests across the Caribbean. Oasis grew into one of Cancún's largest hotel operators, while Pueyo became a Mexican citizen and kept most of his business activity in the region. His business leadership continued throughout his final year. His son Pedro Pueyo Echevarría had held senior Oasis responsibilities, while the distribution of the founder's estate and company shares remained private.

uncertainties.detail: The immutable record says Alive, but multiple contemporaneous sources report Pueyo's death in Madrid on 18 April 2020. Mortality is proposed as a correction; the date components remain review candidates because the initial Alive state categorised their blank fields as inapplicable.

The existing biography is almost entirely vessel history and embeds an Instagram URL. A public-safe, vessel-independent business biography is proposed as a correction rather than treating the nonblank text as usable.

Company and obituary sources use Pedro Pueyo Toldrá, while the immutable record uses the shorter Pedro Pueyo. Toldrá is treated as a second family name in narrative text and is not inserted into the blank middle-names field.

Direct evidence identifies Pedro Pueyo Echevarría as the founder's son and documents his senior Oasis role. No reliable source located establishes the post-death division of Pedro Pueyo Toldrá's estate or company shares, so the son's role is not equated with inherited ownership.

Pueyo was reported as Oasis owner and also had tourism-related property interests, but hotel, airline, agency and real-estate assets held through group companies are not individually attributed as personally titled property.
Pueyo's Royaltur work and airline ventures are historical. Oasis hospitality was his principal interest at death; no present personal role or holding is asserted after 2020.

The immutable record gives Spain, while reporting says his habitual residence followed his Caribbean business interests and he died in Madrid. No residence correction is proposed because public sources do not give a sufficiently precise terminal country-of-residence record.
Vessel context, banking disputes, litigation, allegations, transient valuations and unsupported family-asset allocations are excluded from both biographies.

review.notes: Identity resolves at very high confidence through the full Toldrá surname, Palma birth, Oasis role and Cancún history. The dossier corrects the demonstrably stale living status and vessel-focused biography, distinguishes founder Pedro Pueyo Toldrá from his son Pedro Pueyo Echevarría, and separates personal role from corporate and undisclosed family assets.
